column1: # The daemon flags of the store (P/01.3 N1.3 «Daemon flags»). The table is the source of the flags; the prose refers to it and does not repeat it. A closed set: a flag outside the table or not of its command is a start refusal, code 2 (P/01.3 N4).

# The flag names are those of the prose (--from with two hyphens, as admin_ops writes it). Rows in the order of the prose table; one prose row of three connection limits is three rows. An empty cell is -.
# type — a closed vocabulary: path, dir (directory path), file (file path), addr (host:port), id (member id, P/01.3 N2), bool (no value),
# enum:<a>|<b>…, int:<min>..<max> (max may be empty), bytes:>0 (an integer of bytes, > 0), duration, list:id@addr, list:id@addr/addr.
# default — the default as a machine value (bytes — an integer of bytes; -raft-bind =-raft — the value of another flag; $SERVER_NAME —
# the environment variable of P/02.4 N1.2); default_text — the same as the prose writes it (512KiB, 1MiB); - — no default.
# required and bad are CEL (as write-checks.tsv): required — the flag must be given; bad — a start refusal beyond type and required;
# empty bad — none. commands — the commands at which the flag is admitted: daemon (the start without a subcommand) or a subcommand
# of admin_ops (status, join, leave, admit, backup, restore, import, recover, rights), comma-separated.
# Writing (P/01.3 N1.3, P/01.3-R031): -name value | -name=value; bool — without a value; -- ends the flags; a repeated flag, a bool with a value,
# a positional word of the daemon — a start refusal, code 2; positional words — only of admin_ops by its grammar (admit <id>, backup <file>, leave [id]).
# Values: bytes, int — a decimal integer without a sign, a plus or leading zeros, bytes without a suffix (default_text is the writing of the prose);

# duration — [1-9][0-9]*(ms|s|m|h); addr — a non-empty host (a name, IPv4 or [IPv6]) and a port 1–65535. $SERVER_NAME empty or absent — no default. For -id, the default is used only when required is false; when required is true, the command must explicitly give -id. At daemon/recover startup an effective id must exist: an explicit -id or its allowed nonempty $SERVER_NAME default; otherwise start_flags, exit 2.
# The CEL values of f: int — for int, bytes and an enum of integers; true — for bool; a string as given — for the rest.
#var f map<string,dyn> — the flags parsed from the command line (a flag without a value — true)
#var cmd string — the command: daemon or a subcommand of admin_ops
#fn loopback(string) -> bool — the host of the address is on the loopback: 127.0.0.0/8, ::1 or localhost (normgen prims)

column5: -join in f || "-door" in f || ("-group-size" in f && f["-group-size"] in [3, 5])
column8: P/01.3 N1.3; P/01.3 N2; no -id and no SERVER_NAME — a start refusal (P/01.3 N1.3 daemon refuse_start)
P/01.2 N1.2; without it — only admin.sock, not a refusal (P/01.2 N4)

column5: -join in f || ("-api" in f && !loopback(f["-api"])) || ("-raft" in f && !loopback(f["-raft"])) || ("-api-bind" in f && !loopback(f["-api-bind"])) || ("-raft-bind" in f && !loopback(f["-raft-bind"]))

column7: -raft in f || "-raft-bind" in f || "-bootstrap" in f || "-join" in f || "-group-size" in f

column8: P/01.3-R008: a separate limit per ordinary role socket; P/01.1 N4
